Turner explicitly assigns Gilgit lēl blood to *lōhila-, and under lohita says the Shina word belongs rather to *lōhila-. The l-final branch is diagnostic.
Turner lists Gilgit lōlyu red under *lōhila-, while the lohita article explicitly redirects this Shina form to that l-extended branch.

Turner’s later addenda 14840 and 14845 prefer or suggest *himna- for Shina hin instead of snih-. Both alternatives remain explicitly uncertain; this proposal follows the later preference without treating it as settled.
Turner explicitly assigns Gilgit tušóĭki be filled (of the stomach) to tuṣyati. Entry 5895 instead supplies the past tuṭu; choose the present etymon for this headword.

Turner’s gava article explicitly includes Shina gō, plural gave, and the gō article says direct descent from gauḥ/gām is less likely. The inflected gava stem is the preferred immediate historical base.
Turner explicitly gives Gilgit boĭki become under bhavati; bhūta instead accounts for past bulu. Both source references describe parts of the paradigm, so this stem is assigned to bhavati.

CDIAL 3400 kūpa lists Shina kui valley/inhabited place/village, but the separate addenda cross-refer in both directions: 14393 sends kuṭī to kūpa, while 14402 explicitly suggests kui may derive from kuṭī. Retain kūpa as a provisional comparison rather than treating the first cross-reference as a settled correction; the land/field sense and the competing habitation-word ancestry require review.

Buddruss’s separately collated ajiíno situated above attestation is the same adjective; its source audit also records derivation from ají.

CDIAL 7732 subsection 1 *patta back explicitly gives Shina phatu behind, but questions its aspiration and offers alternative deeper origins from apāñc-related forms or Indo-Iranian *pati. Degener and Buddruss independently attest the behind postposition; their phátu/phatú accent variation is preserved. This assigns the cited Shina family while retaining the unresolved aspiration and remote reconstruction.
